name: <str> Identifier of the underlying Gehring & Homberger instance.
num_customers: <int> Number of customers to be served, excluding the depot.
capacity: <int> Maximum total demand that a single vehicle may carry.
max_vehicles: <int> Hard upper bound on the number of vehicles that may be used. A plan using more vehicles is infeasible.
service_time: <int> Time spent serving each customer, on the scaled integer time axis shared with the time windows and travel times.
coordinates: <list of [<int> x, <int> y]> Location of each node, indexed from 0. Index 0 is the depot; indices 1..num_customers are customers. Travel time and distance between two nodes equal floor(10 * euclidean distance between their coordinates).
demand: <list of <int>> Demand of each node, indexed as in coordinates. The depot has demand 0.
time_window: <list of [<int> earliest, <int> latest]> Interval during which service may begin at each node, indexed as in coordinates. Arriving earlier is allowed and the vehicle waits; arriving later is infeasible. Entry 0 bounds the working day at the depot.
fleet_lower_bound: <int> ceil(sum of demands / capacity), the bin-packing lower bound on the fleet. Equal to max_vehicles here.
